title: System Constraints Awareness
hook: We doubled our leads and revenue didn't move. Onboarding was the real limit the whole time.
statement: Know your limits. Your total output can only be as big as your slowest step.
explainer: Pouring money into the parts that already work does nothing if one step can't keep up. Find the slowest step, and that's where every improvement should go.
sop: Map your business from lead to delivered result.
Write each step's capacity, how many units it handles per day.
Find the lowest number. That's your real limit.
Put this month's whole improvement budget into that one step.
Once it improves, re-map. The limit has probably moved.
equation_example: Sales makes 50 leads a day, Onboarding handles 20, Fulfillment ships 35. Output is the smallest of those Limits, so 20 a day. Higher means your weakest step is getting stronger. Lower means one step is dragging everything down.
question: Write each step's daily capacity and circle the smallest number.
closing_statement: Your weakest link sets your true ceiling.
caption:
Principle Nº 167: System Constraints Awareness

We doubled our leads and revenue didn't move. Onboarding was the real limit the whole time.

Know your limits. Your total output can only be as big as your slowest step.
